Not a PC game, but a Spectrum 48K game: Jet Set Willy.

It had a competition with a prize for the first person to complete it. Unfortunately due to at least three separate game bugs, it was uncompletable.

The prize went to a guy who hacked the game to fix the bugs, and who then finished it. His hack became the official fixes for the game.

Ultima 8 Pagan was basically unplayable at launch because of the platforming (wtf really?) introduced into what had previously been an RPG series. First game I remember that required a patch - and it came on 3.5 floppies.

Ultima 9 was also broken, but for different reason. I was really only QAed with one type of 3D accelerator card. It was non-functional on other types.

Ultima 9 was my first broken PC release. This was back when most publishers included a registration tool with their game, and if you were dialed into the internet, it would send the company your name, address, phone number and the like.

Anyways, EA actually used that info to send everyone a new patched install disk, along with a free copy of Ultima Online as an apology. That's how bad the launch code for Ultima 9 was.

I remember even if a patched state, there were horribly memory leaks that forced you to restart the game, as it slowly ground to a halt the longer you played it.

Man, anybody else remember when more games had crazy bad memory leaks?

I remember a lot of games back in the 90's shipped in some pretty shoddy states. There used to be a huge rush for the holiday season, and then an insane games drought all summer long. I remember as a kid waiting all summer long, reading previews of games over and over again, in print no less, waiting for anything at all to come out.

So every Christmas you'd get a huge flood of buggy games publishers pushed out of the nest, whether they could fly or not. Very few approached the level of No Man's Sky or Arkham Knight where people just dismissed them as being utterly broken nonsense. Somebody already mentioned Ultima 9 which was a pretty bad one.
